# Button

> A standalone action, or a call to action that goes somewhere: a full pill with a large pointer target.

Part of the [Nate Mills Design System](../README.md). It is a CSS class API, not a JavaScript component, so its props are the classes and HTML attributes below. Link the stylesheets as [Getting started](../foundations/getting-started.md) shows, then add the classes. Every component: [Components](README.md).

## When to use

- An action on this page, such as submitting, opening or toggling something.
- A standalone call to action that leaves the page, such as "Read the case study" or "Get in touch".
- An icon-only chrome control, such as a theme toggle or a menu button.

## When not to use

- A destination inside a sentence: use a Link.
- A label or a tag: use a Chip. A status: use a Badge.
- Paging through a carousel: use Carousel navigation.

## Alternatives

- **[Link](link.md):** Words inside running text that take you somewhere are a Link. A standalone action or call to action is a Button.
- **[Chip](chip.md):** A chip only labels and never takes a click. If the thing must do something, it is a Button.
- **[Card](card.md):** A card with one destination becomes that link itself. A card with several actions stays static and puts a Button on each action.
- **[Carousel navigation](carousel-navigation.md):** Paging a carousel is the bare chevrons of Carousel navigation. A labelled action under a carousel is a Button.
- **[Avatar](avatar.md):** Both are circles. An avatar is a person and never acts; an icon button is a control.
- **[Screen-reader text](screen-reader-text.md):** An icon-only Button takes its name from `aria-label`. Screen-reader text adds words to content, not a name to a control.

## How to use

**Element:** `<button type="button">` for an action on this page; `<a href>` for a call to action that goes somewhere.

- Put `.btn` and exactly one variant class on a `<button type="button">` for an action, or on an `<a href>` for a destination.
- For an icon-only control, use `.btn--icon` and give it an `aria-label`.
- Add a size class only for a dense toolbar (`.btn--sm`) or a hero call to action (`.btn--lg`).

**Classes:** `.btn`, `.btn--primary`, `.btn--secondary`, `.btn--icon`, `.btn--sm`, `.btn--md`, `.btn--lg`

## Props

| Prop | Type | Allowed values | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `variant` | modifier class | `primary` (`.btn--primary`), `secondary` (`.btn--secondary`), `icon` (`.btn--icon`) | None. Required: `.btn` alone sets no fill or colour. | How prominent the button is. |
| `size` | modifier class | `sm` (`.btn--sm`), `md` (`.btn--md`), `lg` (`.btn--lg`) | No size class: the base `.btn`, 44px high. | Height and padding. An icon button stays a circle at every size. |
| `type` | attribute | `button`, `submit`, `reset` | `submit`, the HTML default. Set `button` for any action that does not submit a form. | On a `<button>` only. |
| `disabled` | attribute, boolean | present or absent | Absent. | On a `<button>`: dims it, stops pointer input and takes it out of the Tab order. |
| `aria-disabled` | attribute | `true` | Absent. | For a disabled link: set it with `role="link"` and remove the `href`. The button dims the same way. |
| `aria-label` | attribute, string | Text naming the action | None. | Required on the `icon` variant, which has no visible words. |

## Variants

Available variants: `primary`, `secondary`, `icon`.

- `primary` (`.btn--primary`): Lime fill, ink label; inverts to an ink fill on hover. The one main action in a view.
- `secondary` (`.btn--secondary`): Transparent with a grey outline; fills lime on hover. Every other action, and the only one allowed on a lime surface.
- `icon` (`.btn--icon`): A circle holding one glyph and no words; needs an `aria-label`.

Default variant: None. Required: `.btn` alone sets no fill or colour.

Available sizes: `sm`, `md`, `lg`.

- `sm` (`.btn--sm`): 32px high, for dense toolbars and filters only.
- `md` (`.btn--md`): 44px high, with tighter padding than the base.
- `lg` (`.btn--lg`): 52px high, for hero calls to action.

Default size: No size class: the base `.btn`, 44px high.

## States

The CSS styles these states: `:active`, `:disabled`, `:focus`, `:focus-visible`, `:hover`.

## Invalid combinations

Options that must not be used together. Each names the props above.

| Combination | Level | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `variant: primary` with `variant: secondary`, or any two variants on one button | MUST NOT | The rules tie, so the look depends on stylesheet order. |
| `size: sm` with `size: lg`, or any two sizes on one button | MUST NOT | The rules tie, so the height depends on stylesheet order. |
| `.btn` with no `variant` | MUST NOT | The base class sets no fill or colour, so the button renders blank. |
| `variant: primary` on a lime surface | MUST NOT | Lime on lime hides the button. Use `variant: secondary` there. |
| `variant: primary` or `variant: secondary` with a glyph and no words | MUST NOT | An icon-only control is `variant: icon`. |
| `variant: icon` with no `aria-label` | MUST NOT | The button has no visible words, so it would have no name. |

## Keyboard

| Key | Action |
|---|---|
| Tab | Moves focus to the button and shows the focus ring. A `<button disabled>` is skipped. |
| Shift + Tab | Moves focus back to the previous control. |
| Enter | Activates a `<button>`; follows an `<a>`. |
| Space | Activates a `<button>`. On an `<a>` it scrolls the page, as on every link. |

These are the native keys of `<button>` and `<a>`, so they work with no script; the classes change only the look.

## Rules

| Level | Rule | Checked by |
|---|---|---|
| MUST | Keep the pointer target at least 44px. `.btn--sm` at 32px is the one exception, for dense toolbars, and still clears the 24px AA floor. | [Automated: Touch-target lint](../foundations/checks.md#touch-target-lint) |
| MUST | Show the focus ring on keyboard focus; never remove the outline without a replacement. | [Automated: Focus-ring gate](../foundations/checks.md#focus-ring-gate) |
| MUST | Keep the label and glyph readable on hover, focus and press: 4.5:1 for text, 3:1 for an icon. | [Automated: State-contrast gate](../foundations/checks.md#state-contrast-gate) |
| MUST | Give every `.btn--icon` an `aria-label`. | [Automated: axe accessibility scan](../foundations/checks.md#axe-accessibility-scan) |
| MUST | Give a button that leaves the site `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, a trailing `arrow-up-right` glyph and an "opens in a new tab" cue. | [Automated: External-link lint](../foundations/checks.md#external-link-lint) |
| MUST NOT | Put `.btn--primary` on a lime surface. | [Manual: Design review](../foundations/checks.md#design-review) |
| SHOULD | Reach for `.btn--sm` sparingly; it is for dense toolbars, not a default. | [Manual: Design review](../foundations/checks.md#design-review) |

Automated checks run on natemills.me before every publish; the scripts live in the private source repository.

## Do and don't

### Do

- Let `--btn-radius` set every button corner; the theme lab drives that token, so a hardcoded radius breaks the shape tier.
- Use `.btn--icon` for every icon-only control; the base is a real 44px square, and a shrunk consumer restores it with a centred `::after`.
- Build an outbound control as `.btn .btn--secondary` carrying the `arrow-up-right` glyph, never as a hand-rolled pill.
- Let `.btn--icon` take its outline from `--btn-secondary-border`; the glyph names the control, so the edge needs no 3:1 (SC 1.4.11).
- Give a disabled link `aria-disabled`, `role=link` and no `href`, so the strike-through carries what the cursor cannot.

### Don't

- Do not put `.btn--primary` on the lime footer; lime on lime disappears, so `.btn--secondary` is the control there.
- Do not shrink `.btn--primary` down to a single glyph; `.btn--icon` already exists and is round by contract.
- Do not read `.btn--md` as a no-op on the base button; it pads 8px by 16px where the base pads 10px by 18px.
- Do not let `.btn` carry an underline in any state; the rule is held above the global link hover on purpose.
- Do not span a `.btn` full width on mobile outside the two registered places; an unbounded CTA reached 1155px on a tablet.

## Example

```html
<a class="btn btn--primary" href="mailto:mail@natemills.me">Say G'day</a>
<button class="btn btn--icon" type="button" aria-label="Toggle dark mode"><i data-lucide="moon" aria-hidden="true"></i></button>
```

## Look

- **Buttons** are full pills, Work Sans semibold at 14px, padding 10px/18px, default height 44px. The
  primary button is a lime fill with ink label; on hover it inverts to an ink fill with a lime label.
  The secondary button is transparent with a `{colors.border}` outline (a stronger grey in dark) and
  on hover takes the primary's resting look: a lime fill with an ink label.
- **Icon button** is the one canonical circle: a `{colors.border}` hairline ring,
  `{colors.text-primary}` glyph, 44px, `{rounded.full}`, filling lime on hover. Never a pill with a
  label.
- **Action icons** name what the link does: `mail` for a `mailto:` link, `download` for a file
  download, `arrow-up-right` for an external link. Never the `external-link` box glyph, and no icon
  on a same-page anchor, because it never leaves the page.

Values in braces, such as `{colors.border}`, are named on the foundation pages, starting with [Colour](../foundations/color.md); every token with its purpose is on [Tokens](../foundations/tokens.md).

## Recipe

The recipe from [DESIGN.md](../DESIGN.md), one entry per state. Names in braces resolve on the foundation pages.

```yaml
button-primary:
  backgroundColor: "{colors.brand-lime}"
  textColor: "{colors.brand-ink}"
  border: "1px solid {colors.border-brand}"
  typography: "{typography.families.body} at 14px, weight 600, normal tracking, sentence case (not the mono label)"
  rounded: "{rounded.full}"
  padding: "10px 18px"
  height: "44px (md); 32px (sm); 52px (lg)"
button-primary-hover:
  backgroundColor: "{colors.brand-ink}"
  textColor: "{colors.brand-lime}"
button-secondary:
  backgroundColor: "transparent"
  textColor: "{colors.text-primary}"
  border: "1px solid {colors.border} (a stronger grey in dark)"
  rounded: "{rounded.full}"
  padding: "10px 18px"
button-secondary-hover:
  backgroundColor: "{colors.brand-lime}"
  textColor: "{colors.brand-ink}"
  border: "1px solid {colors.border-brand}"
button-icon:
  shape: "circle, {rounded.full}"
  border: "1px solid {colors.border} (a stronger grey in dark)"
  iconColor: "{colors.text-primary}"
  size: "44px, glyph 16px"
  note: "The one canonical icon button. An icon-only button is never a pill with a label."
```

| `.btn` | base | base; always pair with a variant | `--btn-focus-ring`, `--btn-font`, `--btn-font-size`, `--btn-font-weight`, `--btn-gap`, `--btn-pad-x`, `--btn-pad-y`, `--btn-radius`, `--btn-transition`, `--focus-ring-offset`, `--touch-target-min` |

| `.btn--secondary` | modifier | transparent, border-grey outline (stronger grey in dark); fills lime on hover | `--brand-primary-dim`, `--btn-primary-bg`, `--btn-primary-border`, `--btn-primary-fg`, `--btn-secondary-border`, `--btn-secondary-fg` |
| `.btn--icon` | modifier | the one canonical icon button: 44px circle, never a labelled pill | `--brand-primary-dim`, `--btn-icon-border`, `--btn-icon-fg`, `--btn-lg`, `--btn-md`, `--btn-primary-bg`, `--btn-primary-border`, `--btn-primary-fg`, `--btn-radius`, `--btn-sm`, `--touch-target-min` |
